name: Infinite integral (improper integral of the first kind)
name_zh: 无穷积分(第一类瑕积分)
aliases: improper integral of the first kind

definitions.text: If the proper integral $\int_{a}^{b}f(x)dx$ exists for every $b\geq a$, define $I(b)=\int_{a}^{b}f(x)dx$ for each $b\geq a$. The function $I$ is called an infinite integral, or an improper integral of the first kind, denoted $\int_{a}^{\infty}f(x)dx$. The integral converges if $\lim_{b\to+\infty}I(b)$ exists and is finite; otherwise it diverges. If the limit exists and equals $A$, the number $A$ is called the value of the integral, and we write $\int_{a}^{\infty}f(x)dx=A$.
definitions.scope: For $f$ whose proper integral over $[a,b]$ exists for every $b\geq a$; integrals $\int_{-\infty}^{b}f(x)dx$ are defined similarly.

name: Convergence of the integral from minus infinity to infinity

definitions.text: If $\int_{-\infty}^{c}f(x)dx$ and $\int_{c}^{\infty}f(x)dx$ are both convergent for some $c$, the integral $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}f(x)dx$ is convergent, and its value is defined as $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}f(x)dx=\int_{-\infty}^{c}f(x)dx+\int_{c}^{\infty}f(x)dx$ (10.62); the choice of $c$ is unimportant. The integral diverges if at least one of the integrals on the right of (10.62) is divergent.
definitions.scope: Infinite integrals over the entire real line, reduced to two one-sided infinite integrals.

definitions.text: THEOREM 10.23. Assume that the proper integral $\int_{a}^{b}f(x)dx$ exists for each $b\geq a$ and suppose that $f(x)\geq 0$ for all $x\geq a$. Then $\int_{a}^{\infty}f(x)dx$ converges if and only if there is a constant $M>0$ such that $\int_{a}^{b}f(x)dx\leq M$ for every $b\geq a$.

name: Theorem 10.24
name_zh: 定理10.24(瑕积分比较判别法)

definitions.text: THEOREM 10.24. Assume the proper integral $\int_{a}^{b}f(x)dx$ exists for each $b\geq a$ and suppose that $0\leq f(x)\leq g(x)$ for all $x\geq a$, where $\int_{a}^{\infty}g(x)dx$ converges. Then $\int_{a}^{\infty}f(x)dx$ also converges and $\int_{a}^{\infty}f(x)dx\leq\int_{a}^{\infty}g(x)dx$.
definitions.scope: Improper integrals of the first kind with $0\leq f\leq g$; analog of the comparison test for series.

name: Theorem 10.25. Limit comparison test
name_zh: 定理10.25(瑕积分极限比较判别法)

definitions.text: THEOREM 10.25 (LIMIT COMPARISON TEST). Assume both proper integrals $\int_{a}^{b}f(x)dx$ and $\int_{a}^{b}g(x)dx$ exist for each $b\geq a$, where $f(x)\geq 0$ and $g(x)>0$ for all $x\geq a$. If $\lim_{x\to+\infty}f(x)/g(x)=c$ with $c\neq 0$ (10.63), then both integrals $\int_{a}^{\infty}f(x)dx$ and $\int_{a}^{\infty}g(x)dx$ converge or both diverge. Note: If the limit in (10.63) is 0, we can conclude only that convergence of $\int_{a}^{\infty}g(x)dx$ implies convergence of $\int_{a}^{\infty}f(x)dx$.
definitions.scope: Improper integrals of the first kind with $f\geq 0$, $g>0$; analog of the limit comparison test for series.

name: Improper integral of the second kind

definitions.text: Suppose $f$ is defined on the half-open interval $(a,b]$, and assume that $\int_{x}^{b}f(t)dt$ exists for each $x$ satisfying $a<x\leq b$. Define $I(x)=\int_{x}^{b}f(t)dt$ if $a<x\leq b$. The function $I$ so defined is called an improper integral of the second kind, denoted $\int_{a+}^{b}f(t)dt$. The integral converges if $\lim_{x\to a+}I(x)$ exists and is finite; otherwise it diverges. If the limit exists and equals $A$, the number $A$ is called the value of the integral, and we write $\int_{a+}^{b}f(t)dt=A$.
definitions.scope: Finite interval with $f$ unbounded (undefined) at an endpoint; integrals $\int_{a}^{b-}f(t)dt$ are defined in a similar fashion. The convergence tests of Theorems 10.23 through 10.25 have straightforward analogs for this kind.

name: Notation for two-sided and mixed improper integrals
name_zh: 双侧及混合型瑕积分记号

definitions.text: If $\int_{a+}^{c}f(t)dt$ and $\int_{c}^{b-}f(t)dt$ both converge, we write $\int_{a+}^{b-}f(t)dt=\int_{a+}^{c}f(t)dt+\int_{c}^{b-}f(t)dt$. Some authors write $\int_{a}^{b}$ where we have written $\int_{a+}^{b-}$. The definition extends to any finite number of summands (e.g. $f$ undefined at interior points), and to "mixed" combinations such as $\int_{a+}^{b}f(t)dt+\int_{b}^{\infty}f(t)dt$, written $\int_{a+}^{\infty}f(t)dt$.
definitions.scope: Combining improper integrals of the second kind at several points, and mixing first and second kinds over one symbol.

definitions.text: If $s>0$ the integral $\int_{0+}^{\infty}e^{-t}t^{s-1}dt$ converges (interpreted as the sum $\int_{0+}^{1}e^{-t}t^{s-1}dt+\int_{1}^{\infty}e^{-t}t^{s-1}dt$). When $s>0$, this sum is denoted by $\Gamma(s)$. The function $\Gamma$ so defined is called the gamma function, first introduced by Euler in 1729. It has the property that $\Gamma(n+1)=n!$ when $n$ is any integer $\geq 0$; more generally $\Gamma(s+1)=s\Gamma(s)$ (Exercise 19 of Section 10.24).
definitions.scope: Defined for $s>0$ as a mixed improper integral.
